questions.q: What are the three options Tableau offers when it can't place one or more locations on a map?
options: Edit Locations, Filter Data, and Show Data at Default Position
Delete the data source, rebuild the connection, or restart Tableau
Ignore it, crash the workbook, or convert to a filled map automatically
Only one option exists: manually re-typing every value
questions.explain: Tableau's Special Values dialog offers Edit Locations (correct them), Filter Data (exclude them), or Show Data at Default Position (plot them at a default point).

questions.q: When is 'Show Data at Default Position' usually the wrong choice for a real analysis?
options: It silently misrepresents where the unrecognized data actually belongs, since it plots those points at an arbitrary default location
It permanently deletes the unrecognized rows
It's always the best choice in every situation
It only works with filled maps, never symbol maps
questions.explain: Plotting unknowns at a default position hides the problem rather than fixing it — the data appears on the map somewhere misleading rather than correctly or not at all.

questions.q: What can you do for a location that's genuinely unrecognized by Tableau's geocoding database?
options: Manually type in the exact latitude and longitude yourself via the Edit Locations dialog
Nothing — unrecognized locations can never be fixed
Rename the entire data source
Convert the field from a dimension to a measure
questions.explain: The Match values to locations dialog lets you supply exact coordinates directly for a value that isn't in Tableau's built-in database.

questions.q: What makes an ambiguous location different from — and in some ways worse than — an unrecognized one?
options: Tableau silently picks a match without flagging it, so the location might be plotted incorrectly with no visible warning
Ambiguous locations always crash Tableau Desktop
Ambiguous locations are flagged in red exactly like unrecognized ones, with no practical difference
Ambiguous locations only occur with dates, never with geography
questions.explain: An unrecognized location at least raises a visible flag; an ambiguous one (like 'Aberdeen') gets silently resolved to Tableau's best guess, which may be wrong.

questions.q: What's the recommended fix for an ambiguous location like 'Aberdeen,' which exists in multiple places?
options: Add a second geographic field (like State or Country) to the view, giving Tableau enough context to disambiguate correctly
Rename every instance of the city to something unique
Delete all rows containing that city name
There is no fix — ambiguous locations must always be filtered out
questions.explain: Adding a second geographic field gives Tableau the context needed to pick the correct match instead of guessing among several possibilities.
